consistency.rule: every scenario passes every plan check
A builds 94,429 bikes and holds every target from 6 Sep 2027 (the frozen base)
R and R+ build A's bikes, every SKU's total as A's
a build time only delays: no line's date in R earlier than A's, none in R+ earlier than R's; orders cleared A < R < R+
R takes a week from the line to stock on every line; R+ two on the carbon lines and one on the base lines

R+C26: every line closed 21 and 28 Dec 2026; the same bikes on every SKU; only MTB carbon customers wait, none before 4 Jan 2027 (two weeks to build: December's deliveries were on the line before the closure), all delivered by 8 Feb 2027
R+C26: lines full before the closure cannot build ahead; road base, the one with room, builds ahead exactly what R+ builds in the closed weeks
R+E4 builds exactly the 300 it adds, all RW-4418; other lines identical; only MTB carbon customers wait; MTB carbon at target 1 week later, orders cleared 2 weeks later

R+E5 builds RW-9304 only in whole lots of 50, its total rounded up to a whole lot (16,267 -> 16,300); other lines identical; no line's date moves; the line never short of capacity in a week R+ ran it full
R+E5: the lots' cost to customers is 3 RW-9304 bikes a week late (11 Jan 2027), so orders clear 18 Jan
R+P1 builds R+'s bikes, holds every line's target on R+'s date, clears every order on R+'s date, the same fill

R+P1 brings RW-9304 (31 May 2027) and RW-4418 (13 Sep) to target sooner, RW-6416 on R+'s date; it moves MTB carbon, and road carbon (its first step, orders past their date, covers every line); base lines identical
a change never brings a line's date earlier than R+'s
every scenario delivers the most any plan could by every week, on every line, every solve certified; with lots, within the bikes the lots cost (R+E5: 3)

_meta.optimality: every solve certified from its duals and re-solved by interior point (tests/test_optimality.py); every optimal plan is the solver's plan to within what the solver's tolerance buys, under 2 bikes (tests/test_engine.py, no ties)
_meta.deliveries: every scenario: at every week and on every line, the fewest units any plan could leave owed, solved and certified, equals the plan's; R+E5 within 3 bikes in one week, the cost of lots (scenarios.most_delivered; tests/test_r_cases.py)

mechanism.R+E4: demand added on a full line
mechanism.R+P1: a change to what the plan values

story.why: A ships a bike the week it is built; no plant does. R is A with a week to build. R+ gives the carbon lines two weeks and the base lines one; it is the build plan. Neither build time is in the data.
story.pruned: B, B+E3, E1-E5 and P1 on A, a November line-down and a 2027 Christmas closure on R+: each showed nothing the final set does not (docs/WORKING_NOTES.md D28). They stay in the code, not here.

_meta.tests: run PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q to confirm the suite that pins these numbers
